runs.summary: Data through Aug 7 (Q3 partial). Top 3: SMH +61.8%, CIBR +37.3%, XLK +30.9%. SPY P/E: 26.82x (unchanged)
runs.content:
Top 5 YTD 2026: SMH +61.8% (P/E 44.71x, Expensive), CIBR +37.3% (33.92x, Elevated), XLK +30.9% (37.37x, Expensive), XLE +30.4% (20.94x, Fair), XBI +29.2% (P/E N/A).

Bottom 5 YTD 2026: XLC -5.0% (15.14x, Fair), GLD +0.6% (P/E N/A), XLY +0.8% (28.17x, Elevated), XLU +3.5% (22.88x, Fair), GDX +4.8% (13.56x, Cheap).

Notable shifts: a sharp precious-metals/mining rally in the week ended Aug 7 flipped GDX from -13.6% to +4.8% YTD and XME from -2.7% to +11.9% — the largest swings in the tracker — with GLD also turning positive (+0.6%, from -6.3%). That leaves zero sectors in the 'Reversing' bucket for the first time this year. CIBR broke out as the top non-commodity mover, its Q3 partial accelerating to +8.9% (from +2.2%) and pulling YTD from +28.9% to +37.3%. On the flip side, XLE and AMLP — the prior run's clearest momentum leaders — both pulled back this week (XLE +35.0%→+30.4%, AMLP +22.3%→+20.2%), the only two sectors with declining YTD despite a broadly rallying market. XLY crossed into positive YTD (+0.8%, from -2.4%) for the first time in 2026. Data quality note: all 25 P/E figures came back unchanged from the prior run — a clean, stable read with zero valuation band crossings.

runs.content:

Bottom 5 YTD 2026: GDX -13.6% (13.56x, Cheap), XLC -7.5% (15.14x, Fair), GLD -6.3% (P/E N/A), XME -2.7% (19.94x, Fair), XLY -2.4% (28.17x, Elevated).

Notable shifts: CIBR crossed the only valuation band this run (Expensive→Elevated, 35.25x→33.92x) as its Q3 partial reversed from -1.6% to +2.2%, pulling YTD back up from +24.0% to +28.9% — undoing last run's 'Fading' flag. XLU broke its steady 'Continuing' pattern with its first negative quarter of 2026 (Q3 -2.2%), pulling YTD down from +9.9% to +5.3%. XLY, XLC and XRT all showed clear stabilization after deepening declines in the prior run: XLY's YTD loss narrowed from -8.0% to -2.4%, XLC's from -9.2% to -7.5%, and XRT flipped back to positive momentum (+5.8% YTD, from +2.5%). GDX remains by far the tracker's worst YTD performer and deteriorated further (-13.6%, from -12.3%). Data quality note: all 25 P/E figures moved from the prior run — genuine fresh valuation data, unlike the stale/byte-identical reads flagged two runs ago, and SPY's P/E finally returned a plausible figure (26.82x) instead of a garbled value.
